endorsements.quote: We propose systematic testing of ethically sensitive prompts and thorough chain-of-thought analysis to ensure safe, trustworthy deployment in healthcare.

First, similar to Baker et al. approach 2, systematically vary ethically charged variables (e.g., patient prognosis, resource scarc ity) to pinpoint where the model ’s reasoning suggests impermissibl e actions.
With increased mode l complexity and rapid iteration, scalable and reliable post-deployment monitoring solutions will be crucial.
Chang et al.1 rightly note that each new model version may regress or introduce new errors, necessitating continuous re-evaluation.

unlisted_practices: Analyze chain-of-thought reasoning of LLMs to identify manipulative or unethical rationales before they influence the final output.
Do not red-team only final LLM outputs; also audit intermediate reasoning steps.
Formalize ongoing audits of ethical risk areas for deployed LLMs.
Staff LLM audits with multidisciplinary teams of clinicians, ethicists, developers, regulatory compliance experts, and patient advocates, supported by automated evaluation and explainability tools.
Establish accountability structures assigning clear oversight and regular reporting responsibilities to maintain ongoing ethical and safety standards.

screen.reason: This is a letter/commentary proposing reasoning red teaming and monitoring chain-of-thought in LLMs to ensure safe healthcare deployment, rather than an empirical evaluation.
